<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917894_theRebbe_634" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917894_theRebbe_634__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains why the verse says "as the days of your going out from Egypt" in plural, because it includes both the Exodus and the Splitting of the Sea.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the precise point is known</t>
    <t s="2">regarding what is written, "as the days of your going out from the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="3">"days" being plural,</t>
    <t s="4">yet the Exodus from Egypt occurred on a single day</t>
    <t s="5">[and regarding the remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt it is written, "Remember this day on which you went out from Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="6">"so that you remember the day of your going out from the land of Egypt"],</t>
    <t s="7">so why is it said "as the days," in the plural?</t>
    <t s="8">And one may offer the explanation of this,</t>
    <t s="9">that the Exodus from Egypt also includes the Splitting of the Sea.</t>
    <t s="10">[And so it is regarding the commandment to remember the Exodus from Egypt every day,</t>
    <t s="11">that it also includes the remembrance of the Splitting of the Sea.</t>
    <t s="12">And likewise regarding the commandment to recount the Exodus from Egypt on the night of Passover,</t>
    <t s="13">that whoever expands upon recounting the Exodus from Egypt is praiseworthy,</t>
    <t s="14">for the recounting of the Splitting of the Sea is also included in this.]</t>
    <t s="15">Therefore it is said, "as the days of your going out from the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="16">"days" in the plural.</t>
    <t s="17">[And what is written in the commandment to remember the Exodus from Egypt, "the day of your going out from the land of Egypt," is</t>
    <t s="18">because the essence of the commandment to remember the Exodus from Egypt is the remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt itself, and the remembrance of the Splitting of the Sea is not indispensable.]</t>
    <t s="19">And the interpretation of "as the days of your going out from the land of Egypt I will show him wonders" is,</t>
    <t s="20">that in the future redemption there will be the miracles and wonders that occurred in the Exodus from Egypt itself, and also the miracle and wonder of the Splitting of the Sea.</t>
    <t s="21">As it is written,</t>
    <t s="22">"And Hashem will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea... and there will be a highway... as there was for Israel on the day of their ascent from the land of Egypt."</t>
    <t s="23">And one must understand the connection of these two matters in "as the days of your going out from the land of Egypt I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="24">that even the wonders drawn from Him, blessed be He, alone will be in a manner of "I will show him"</t>
    <t s="25">(that they will see the miracle within them),</t>
    <t s="26">and that in the wonders that will be in the future redemption there will also be the wonder of the Splitting of the Sea.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the root of miracles clothed in nature is from a higher place than miracles above nature, because they reveal the limitless within the world itself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing,</t>
    <t s="2">that the root of miracles clothed in nature is from a more elevated place than the root of miracles that are above nature,</t>
    <t s="3">that is,</t>
    <t s="4">for in miracles that are above nature,</t>
    <t s="5">the revelation of Ein Sof, blessed be He, which is above worlds</t>
    <t s="6">(from which the miracles are drawn)</t>
    <t s="7">is in a manner that nature is nullified by the revelation,</t>
    <t s="8">through the overturning of the natural order,</t>
    <t s="9">and consequently,</t>
    <t s="10">the revelation is not drawn into the world.</t>
    <t s="11">But in miracles clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="12">the revelation of Ein Sof, blessed be He, which is above worlds, is within the world itself.</t>
    <t s="13">And since the world itself is limitation,</t>
    <t s="14">and limitation and the limitless are two opposites,</t>
    <t s="15">therefore,</t>
    <t s="16">in order for the revelation of Ein Sof, blessed be He, to be within the limitation of the world,</t>
    <t s="17">it is through the drawing down of the limitless from the Essence of Ein Sof, which is present in every place, even within the limitation</t>
    <t s="18">(and nature)</t>
    <t s="19">of the world.</t>
    <t s="20">And there is further explanation of the superiority of miracles clothed in nature over miracles above nature,</t>
    <t s="21">that the concept of miracles is that through them it is revealed that He, blessed be He, rules and dominates over nature.</t>
    <t s="22">And this concept is revealed more in miracles clothed in nature.</t>
    <t s="23">For the revelation of His dominion, blessed be He, through miracles above nature is that He has the power to nullify and overturn the laws of nature,</t>
    <t s="24">but in miracles clothed in nature it is revealed that Ein Sof rules and dominates over nature itself,</t>
    <t s="25">that nature should be according to His will.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between two explanations of the superiority of miracles clothed in nature, through the concept that the constancy of nature reveals the limitless power of the Creator.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the difference between the two explanations of the superiority of miracles clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="2">will be understood by prefacing what is said in the Akeidah,</t>
    <t s="3">that even from the conduct of nature one can know the greatness of the Creator.</t>
    <t s="4">For in addition to the fact that through contemplation of the conduct of creation</t>
    <t s="5">(the movement of the constellations, etc.)</t>
    <t s="6">one comes to recognize that there is a Master of this palace,</t>
    <t s="7">behold, through contemplation of the fact that the conduct of nature is constant without change,</t>
    <t s="8">and in the language of the verse,</t>
    <t s="9">"they shall not cease,"</t>
    <t s="10">that although it has been nearly six thousand years, nevertheless there is no weakening in the natural conduct,</t>
    <t s="11">[and likewise from the fact that throughout all this time no weakening has occurred in the power of the creations,</t>
    <t s="12">for that the host of heaven endures as individuals and the host of earth endures as species is in a manner that they are as strong as on the day of their creation],</t>
    <t s="13">through this one knows the greatness of the Creator,</t>
    <t s="14">that His power, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="15">(from which the influence comes into the world)</t>
    <t s="16">is infinite and limitless.</t>
    <t s="17">For although the nature of creations is from the G-dly vitality that is clothed within them,</t>
    <t s="18">and that each creation has its particular nature is according to the manner of the vitality within it,</t>
    <t s="19">from which it is understood that the vitality clothed in the creations is limited vitality,</t>
    <t s="20">behold, this is regarding nature itself,</t>
    <t s="21">but the constancy in the conduct of nature,</t>
    <t s="22">that there is no change or weakening in it,</t>
    <t s="23">is through the power of the infinite, limitless One, which is above clothing.</t>
    <t s="24">However, in order to know the greatness of the Creator through the conduct of nature,</t>
    <t s="25">contemplation is required.</t>
    <t s="26">But when one sees a miracle,</t>
    <t s="27">a change in nature,</t>
    <t s="28">one sees immediately</t>
    <t s="29">(even without contemplation)</t>
    <t s="30">that this comes from Ein Sof, who is not limited by the boundaries of the world.</t>
    <t s="31">And there is a further superiority in miracles over the conduct of nature,</t>
    <t s="32">that the power of the infinite, limitless One that is revealed through the constancy in the conduct of nature</t>
    <t s="33">(even after contemplation)</t>
    <t s="34">is clothed in the matter of limitation,</t>
    <t s="35">for the conduct of nature</t>
    <t s="36">(limitation)</t>
    <t s="37">has no change or cessation,</t>
    <t s="38">but through miracles, the revelation of Ein Sof, the limitless One Himself, which is above clothing in limitation, is drawn down.</t>
    <t s="39">Nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="40">for this very reason,</t>
    <t s="41">there is a superiority in the revelation of the power of Ein Sof that is revealed through the constancy in the conduct of nature over the revelation of Ein Sof through miracles.</t>
    <t s="42">For the matter of the limitless as it is revealed through miracles,</t>
    <t s="43">the overturning of the world's nature,</t>
    <t s="44">is not connected to the world,</t>
    <t s="45">but through the constancy in the conduct of nature,</t>
    <t s="46">it is revealed that even the vitality of the world</t>
    <t s="47">(limitation)</t>
    <t s="48">is connected with Ein Sof, the limitless One.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
